en: One chosen or set apart.
In Calvinist theology, one foreordained to Heaven. In other Christian theologies, someone chosen by God for salvation.
To choose or make a decision (to do something).
(Of a group) to officially select one or more candidates in an election to hold office.
Who has been elected in a specified post, but has not yet entered office.
Chosen; taken by preference from among two or more.

elect.ety:
Borrowed from Latin ēlēctus, past participle of ēligō (“to pick out, choose, elect”), from ē- (“out”) + legō (“to pick out, pick, gather, collect, etc.”); see legend.
Cognate to eclectic, which is via Ancient Greek rather than Latin, hence prefix ἐκ (ek), rather than e- (from ex).

ex.en: They elected John the captain of the team.
ex.ja: 彼らはジョンをチームのキャプテンにした。

ex.en: He has a good chance of being elected.
ex.ja: 彼は当選の見込みが十分ある。

ex.en: There's a good chance that he'll be elected.
ex.ja: 彼は当選の見込みが十分ある。

note.ja: e（外へ）+ lect（選ぶ）。選び出す →「選挙で選ぶ」。

en: Untrue, not factual, factually incorrect.
Based on factually incorrect premises.
To incorrectly decode noise as if it were a valid signal.
To begin a race before being instructed to do so; to do a false start.
In a dishonest and disloyal way; falsely.
One of two options on a true-or-false test, that not representing true.

false.ety:
From Middle English false, fals, from Old English fals (“false; counterfeit; fraudulent; wrong; mistaken”), from Latin falsus (“counterfeit, false; falsehood”), perfect passive participle of fallō (“deceive”). Reinforced in Middle English by Anglo-Norman and Old French fals, faus. Compare Scots fals, false, Saterland Frisian falsk, German falsch, Dutch vals, Swedish and Danish falsk; all from Latin falsus. Displaced native Middle English les, lese, from Old English lēas (“false”); See lease, leasing. Doublet of faux.
The verb is from Middle English falsen, falsien, from Old French falser, from

ex.en: What she said turned out to be false.
ex.ja: 彼女が言ったことが嘘であることがわかった。

ex.en: He made a false statement to the police.
ex.ja: 彼は警察に偽りの申し立てをした。

ex.en: What he said turned out to be false.
ex.ja: 彼の説明は誤りであると判明した。

note.ja: ラテン語 falsus（だまされた・偽の）から。fallere（だます）。fail、fault と同じ。

en: To establish the identity of someone or something.
To disclose the identity of someone.

identify.ety: From French identifier, from Medieval Latin identicus + Latin faciō.

ex.en: The lost boy was identified by his clothes.
ex.ja: 行方不明だった少年は服で身元が確認された。

ex.en: Can you identify the man using this picture?
ex.ja: 写真でその男性が誰か分かりますか。

ex.en: You can identify children's voices without any problem.
ex.ja: 子供の声はたやすく識別できる。

note.ja: ラテン語 identicus（同一の）+ -ify。idem（同じ）。「同じものだと確かめる」→「特定する」。identity と同じ。

en: Too implausible to be credible; beyond belief.
Amazing; astonishing; awe-inspiring.

incredible.ety: From Middle English incredible, from Latin incrēdibilis (“that cannot be believed”), from in- (“not”) + crēdibilis (“worthy of belief”), from crēdō (“believe”), equivalent to in- + credible.

ex.en: That story is too incredible to be true.
ex.ja: あの話には信じられないところが多すぎて本当とは思えない。

ex.en: The waste of time and money is incredible.
ex.ja: 時間とお金の浪費はとてつもない。

ex.en: At this hour, there is incredible traffic.
ex.ja: この時間帯は交通量が非常に多い。

note.ja: in（否定）+ cred（信じる）+ ible（できる）。信じられない →「信じられない・すごい」。

ex.en: What inspired you to write this song?
ex.ja: この曲を書こうと思ったきっかけは何だったの？

ex.ja: 友人に触発されてブログなるものを始めてみました。

ex.ja: 私は生徒たちにもっと勉強するよう励ました。

en: mother, mama
The landlady of a theater.

ma.ety: The sound, which parents interpret as a reference to themselves, is very commonly made by infants. For more on the linguistic process whereby infants' monosyllables are tied to ancient word roots for parents, see mama, papa, mātēr, and patēr.

en: The flesh (muscle tissue) of a killed animal used as food.
A food designed to replicate its taste and texture (such as plant-based meat).

ex.ja: あなた方が肉を食べない理由をどうぞ教えてください。

ex.ja: 肉と魚どちらが好きですか。

ex.en: The price of meat will soon come down.
ex.ja: 肉の値段はやがて下がるだろう。

note.ja: 古英語 mete（食べ物）から。昔は食べ物全般を指した。sweetmeat（甘い食べ物）に名残がある。

en: A government department at the administrative level, normally headed by a minister (or equivalent rank, e.g. secretary of state), who hol…
The complete body of government ministers (whether or not they are in cabinet) under the leadership of a head of government (such as a pr…

ministry.ety: From Middle English mynisterie, borrowed from Old French menistere, in turn borrowed itself from Latin ministerium; equivalent to minister + -y.

ex.en: Finance Ministry officials tried to boost confidence in recovery.
ex.ja: 大蔵省の役人は景気回復への信頼をより高めようとしました。

ex.en: My father serves in the Foreign Ministry.
ex.ja: 私の父は外務省に勤めている。

ex.en: The ministry administers the internal affairs.
ex.ja: その省は内政問題の行政をつかさどる。

note.ja: minister（大臣）+ -ry。「大臣の職」→「省」。

en: A particular means of accomplishing something.
A state related to signals or vibrations.

mode.ety: From Old French mode (masculine), from Latin modus (“measure, due measure, rhythm, melody”). Doublet of modus.

ex.en: Tom usually keeps his phone in manner mode.
ex.ja: トムは普段、携帯電話をマナーモードにしている。

ex.en: Please set your cell phones to silent mode.
ex.ja: 携帯をマナーモードに設定してください。

ex.en: Did you set your phone to airplane mode?
ex.ja: 携帯は、機内モードにした？

en: The part of the body connecting the head and the trunk found in humans and some animals.
The corresponding part in some other anatomical contexts.
To intently kiss or cuddle; to canoodle.
To decrease in diameter.

ex.en: The kid is a pain in the neck.
ex.ja: あの子にはうんざりする。

ex.en: The fact is I'm up to my neck.
ex.ja: アップアップ状態です。

ex.en: He got his neck broken in the accident.
ex.ja: 彼はその事故で首を痛めた。

note.ja: 古英語 hnecca から。「首」。

en: Newly made, formed or evolved; having no precedent; of recent origin; new.
Original, especially in an interesting way; new and striking; not of the typical or ordinary type.
A work of prose fiction, longer than a novella.
A fable; a short tale, especially one of many making up a larger work.

novel.ety: From Middle English novel, from Old French novel (“new, fresh, recent, recently made or done, strange, rare”) (modern nouvel, nouveau), from Latin novellus (“new, fresh, young, modern”), diminutive of novus (“new”). Doublet of nouveau.

ex.en: I spent the whole day reading that novel.
ex.ja: 私は１日中その小説を読んで過ごした。

ex.en: His new novel will come out next month.
ex.ja: 彼の新作の小説は来月出版される。

ex.en: What do you think of his new novel?
ex.ja: 彼の新作の小説をどう思いますか。

note.ja: ラテン語 novus（新しい）から。nov + el。新しい →「斬新な」、新しい物語 →「（長編）小説」。innovation（新しくすること→革新）も同じ。

en: Easily discovered, seen, or understood; self-explanatory.

obvious.ety: 16th century, from Latin obvius (“being in the way so as to meet, meeting, easy to access, at hand, ready, obvious”) + -ous, from ob- (“before”) + via (“way”).

ex.en: It is obvious that that is a lie.
ex.ja: 嘘に決まってんじゃん。

ex.en: I think it's pretty obvious Tom likes Mary.
ex.ja: トムがメアリーを好きなのは明らかだと思うよ。

ex.en: The reason he refused your offer is obvious.
ex.ja: 彼が君の申し出を断った理由は明白だ。

en: An article of clothing that is worn on the upper part of the body, often with sleeves that cover some or all of the arms.
An interior lining in a blast furnace.
To cover or clothe with a shirt, or as if with a shirt.

ex.en: What shirt will you wear to school today?
ex.ja: 今日はどのシャツを着て学校へ行くつもり？

ex.en: A button on your shirt is falling off.
ex.ja: シャツのボタン、取れかかってるよ。

note.ja: 古英語 scyrte から。short（短い）と同じ語根で、skirt とも同じ語源。

en: At a slow pace.

slowly.ety: From Middle English slowly, slowli, slouli, slowliche, from Old English slāwlīċe (“slowly; sluggishly”), equivalent to slow + -ly. Compare Old Norse slæliga, sljóliga.

ex.en: We had to drive slowly all the way.
ex.ja: 私達は道すがらずっと低速で運転しなければならなかった。

ex.en: He walked slowly so the child could follow.
ex.ja: 彼はその子供がついてこられるようにゆっくり歩いた。

ex.en: The old lady walked slowly up the hill.
ex.ja: その老婦人はゆっくりと丘を歩いて登った。

note.ja: slow（遅い）+ -ly。「ゆっくりと」。

en: A venue where sporting events are held.
An Ancient Greek racecourse, especially, the Olympic course for foot races.

stadium.ety: From Latin stadium (“a measure of length, a race course”) (commonly one-eighth of a Roman mile; translated in early English Bibles by furlong), from Ancient Greek στάδιον (stádion, “a measure of length, a running track”), especially the track at Olympia, which was one stadium in length. The Greek word may literally mean "fixed standard of length" (from στάδιος (stádios, “firm, fixed”), from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂-, whence also stand and Latin stare). Doublet of stade, stadion, and estadio. Displaced native Old English spyrd.

ex.en: There were lots of people in the stadium.
ex.ja: スタジアムには大勢の人がいた。

ex.en: I cannot go to the stadium by myself.
ex.ja: 私は一人でスタジアムに行けません。

ex.en: There were a lot of people in the stadium.
ex.ja: 球場には多くの人たちがいた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 stadion（約185mの長さの単位）から。その長さの競走路 →「競技場」。

ex.ja: 手術をしないといけないんでしょうか？

en: The third day of the week in many religious traditions, and the second day of the week in systems that use the ISO 8601 norm; it follows …
On Tuesday.

Tuesday.ety:
From Middle English Tewesday, from Old English tīwesdæġ (“Tuesday”), from Proto-West Germanic *Tīwas dag (“Tuesday”, literally “Tiw's Day”), equivalent to Tiu + -s- + day.
This was a Germanic interpretation of Latin diēs Mārtis, itself a translation of Ancient Greek Ἄρεως ἡμέρα (Áreōs hēméra) (interpretatio romana). Cognate with Scots Tysday (“Tuesday”), Saterland Frisian Täisdai (“Tuesday”), West Frisian tiisdei (“Tuesday”), dialectal German Ziestag (“Tuesday”), Danish tirsdag (“Tuesday”), Swedish tisdag (“Tuesday”), Finnish tiistai (“Tuesday”). More at Tyr, day.

ex.en: Today is the last Tuesday of the month.
ex.ja: 今日は今月最後の火曜日です。

ex.en: "Is it Monday or Tuesday?" "Today is Tuesday."
ex.ja: 「月曜だっけ、火曜だっけ？」「今日は、火曜日よ」

ex.en: We have to finish everything before Tuesday morning.
ex.ja: 火曜の朝までにすべて終えなければならないのです。

note.ja: 古英語 Tīwesdæg（戦いの神ティウの日）。ラテン語 dies Martis（マルスの日）を置き換えた。

en: The sense or ability of sight.
Something seen; an object perceived visually.
To imagine something as if it were to be true.
To present as in a vision.

ex.en: Do you have a vision of your future?
ex.ja: あなたは自分の将来のビジョンを持っていますか。

ex.en: I have some damage to my vision.
ex.ja: 視力障害があります。

ex.en: The vision of the Olympics had kept him going.
ex.ja: オリンピックへの夢が彼を支えていた。

note.ja: vis（見る）+ ion。見ること →「視力・展望・幻」。

en: At any time that.
At the (single) time that, no matter when.
At any time.

whenever.ety: From Middle English whan evere, whanne ever, whanne evere, whener, when ever; equivalent to when + -ever.

ex.en: Call me up whenever you need my help.
ex.ja: 私の助けが必要ならいつでも電話してください。

ex.en: You will find him home whenever you call.
ex.ja: いつ来ても彼に会えるよ。

ex.en: Whenever you come, I'll play Go with you.
ex.ja: いつ来てくれても、碁の相手をしますよ。

note.ja: when（いつ）+ ever（いつでも）。「〜するときはいつでも」。

en: The cardinal number occurring before one and that denotes no quantity or amount at all, represented in Arabic numerals as 0.
The numeric symbol that represents the cardinal number zero.
The digit 0 in the decimal, binary, and all other base numbering systems.
Synonym of no.
Of a cloud ceiling, limiting vision to 50 feet (15 meters) or less.
Of horizontal visibility, limited to 165 feet (50.3 meters) or less.

zero.ety: Collectively borrowed from Early Modern Spanish zero, Middle French zero, and (their etymon) Old Italian zero, from Medieval Latin zēphirum, from Arabic صِفْر (ṣifr, “nothing; cipher”), itself calqued from Sanskrit शून्य (śūnyá, “void; nothingness”). Doublet of cipher and chiffre. Cognate with Spanish cero and French zéro.

ex.en: It was ten degrees below zero this morning.
ex.ja: 今朝の気温は零下１０度であった。

ex.en: We had to start our business from zero.
ex.ja: 私たちは商売をゼロから始めなければならなかった。

ex.en: The temperature has fallen below zero this morning.
ex.ja: 今朝は気温が氷点下に下がっている。

note.ja: アラビア語 ṣifr（空）からイタリア語 zefiro を経た語。cipher と同じ語源。

Someone who is chosen to represent a group of people in a contest.
Acting as a champion; having defeated all one's competitors.
Excellent; beyond compare.
To promote, advocate, or act as a champion for (a cause, etc.).

en: The butterfat or milkfat part of milk which rises to the top; this part when separated from the remainder.
The liquid separated from milk, possibly with certain other milk products added, and with at least eighteen percent of it milkfat.
Cream-coloured; having a yellowish white colour.
To puree, to blend with a liquifying process.
To turn a yellowish white color; to give something the color of cream.

cream.ety:

en: A crucial or decisive point or situation; a turning point.
An unstable situation, in political, social, economic or military affairs, especially one involving an impending abrupt change.

crisis.ety: From Latin crisis, from Ancient Greek κρίσις (krísis, “a separating, power of distinguishing, decision, choice, election, judgment, dispute”), from κρίνω (krínō, “pick out, choose, decide, judge”).

ex.en: People are saying that the crisis is over.
ex.ja: 人々が危機は去ったと言っています。

ex.en: In a crisis you must keep your head.
ex.ja: 危機の時は落ち着かなければならない。

ex.en: You must know you're faced with a crisis.
ex.ja: 君は危機に直面していることを知らねばならんよ。

en: To set free from restraint or danger.
To assist in the birth of.

deliver.ety:

ex.ja: 1週間以内にお届けします。

ex.en: Come what may, the mail will get delivered.
ex.ja: どんなことがあろうとも、郵便は配達されるだろう。

First attested in the 15th century from Middle English alcofol, from Middle French alcohol or Spanish alcohol, derived from the Medieval Latin rendering alcohol transmitted in medical or alchemical literature of Arabic اَلْكُحْل (al-kuḥl, “kohl”), which in Andalusian Arabic also bore the form كُحُول (kuḥūl), قُحُول (quḥūl); bearing thus the meaning of stibnite first, then generalized in meaning to a powde

ex.en: This beer has a high content of alcohol.
ex.ja: このビールは、アルコール度数が高い。

ex.en: "My father doesn't drink alcohol." "Mine doesn't either."
ex.ja: 「僕の父は酒を飲みません」「私の父もなんです」

ex.en: What kind of alcohol do you usually drink?
ex.ja: 普段飲むお酒の種類は何ですか？

note.ja: アラビア語 al-kuḥl（アイシャドウ用の粉）から。「精製された粉」→「精製された液体」→「アルコール」。

en: A set of pieces that work together in unison as a mechanism or device.
The act or process of putting together a set of pieces, fragments, or elements.

assembly.ety: From Middle English assemblee, from Anglo-Norman asemblee (Old French asemblee, French assemblée). By surface analysis, assemble + -y.

ex.en: Tom works on an assembly line.
ex.ja: トムは組立ラインで働いている。

ex.en: There were a great many people present at the assembly.
ex.ja: その集会に多くの人が出席した。

ex.en: Japan stood with the United States at the U. N. Assembly.
ex.ja: 日本は国連総会で米国側に立った。

note.ja: as（〜へ）+ sembl（一緒に・似た）+ y。ひとつに集めること →「集会・議会・組み立て」。assemble（集める・組み立てる）。

en: The first meal of the day, usually eaten in the morning.
A meal consisting of food normally eaten in the morning, which may typically include eggs, sausages, toast, bacon, etc.
To eat the morning meal.
To serve breakfast to.

breakfast.ety: From Middle English brekefast, brekefaste, equivalent to break + fast (literally, "to end the nightly fast"), likely a variant of Old English fæstenbryċe, (literally, "fast-breach"). Cognate with Dutch breekvasten (“breakfast”).

ex.en: I used to take a walk before breakfast.
ex.ja: 私は朝食前によく散歩したものだった。

ex.en: George had a lot of cheese for breakfast.
ex.ja: ジョージは朝にたくさんのチーズを食べた。

ex.en: I thought Tom would make breakfast for us.
ex.ja: トムが朝ご飯を作ってくれるって思ってたのに。

note.ja: break（破る）+ fast（断食）。夜の間の「断食を破る」食事。dinner と同じ発想。

en: Emitting much light; visually dazzling; luminous, lucent, radiant.
Of light: brilliant, intense.
Something (especially a product intended for sale) that has vivid colours or a lustrous appearance.
A person with a naturalistic worldview with no mystical or supernatural elements.
In a bright manner; brightly, glowingly, luminously, lustrously.
Referring to colour: with bold or vivid colours; brightly, boldly, vividly.

bright.ety:
The adjective is from Middle English bright, from Old English berht, beorht, bryht, byrht, from Proto-West Germanic *berht, from Proto-Germanic *berhtaz (“bright”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰerHǵ- (“to gleam, shine, whiten”).
The noun is derived from Middle English bright (“brightness, brilliance; daylight; light”), from bright (adjective): see above.
Cognates
Cognate with Scots bricht (“bright”), Danish bjært (“bright”), Faroese and Icelandic bjartur (“bright”), Norwegian Nynorsk bjart (“bright”), Swedish bjärt (“bright”), Gothic 𐌱𐌰𐌹𐍂𐌷𐍄𐍃 (bairhts, “bright, clear; evident”); also

ex.en: She is not only pretty, but also bright.
ex.ja: 彼女はきれいなばかりでなく、利口だ。

ex.en: He is what we call a bright boy.
ex.ja: 彼はいわゆる秀才である。

ex.en: He is not less bright than his brother.
ex.ja: 彼は兄に劣らず頭がいい。

note.ja: 古英語 beorht（輝く）から。「明るい」→「利口な」。

en: Able and efficient; having the ability needed for a specific task; having the disposition to do something; permitting or being susceptibl…

capable.ety: Borrowed from Middle French capable, from Late Latin capābilis.

ex.en: Who do you believe is the most capable?
ex.ja: 誰が一番有能だと思いますか。

ex.en: Jane is not capable of learning from experience.
ex.ja: ジェーンは経験から学ぶ能力がない。

ex.en: The man is quite capable of telling lies.
ex.ja: 奴はうそもつきかねない男だ。

note.ja: cap（つかむ）+ able。つかむことができる →「能力がある・〜できる」。capacity（収容力・能力）も同じ。

en: The act of combining, the state of being combined or the result of combining.
An object formed by combining.

combination.ety:
PIE word
 *dwóh₁
From Middle English combinacioun, combynacyoun, from Old French combination, from Late Latin combīnātiō. Morphologically combine + -ation.

ex.en: A combination of parties formed the new government.
ex.ja: 党が連合して、新しい政府となった。

ex.en: Don't you think that's a good combination?
ex.ja: いい取り合わせだと思わない？

ex.en: A combination of several mistakes led to the accident.
ex.ja: いくつかのミスが重なってその事故が起こった。

note.ja: combine（組み合わせる）+ -ation。com + bini（2つずつ）。「組み合わせ」。

en: A person who favors maintenance of the status quo.
One who seeks to promote or preserve traditional values or institutions.
Cautious, moderate.
Tending to resist change or innovation.

conservative.ety: Borrowed from Middle French conservatif, from Latin cōnservō (“to preserve”). Equivalent to conserve + -ative.

ex.en: On the whole, the Japanese are conservative.
ex.ja: 概して、日本人は保守的である。

ex.en: The English are generally a conservative people.
ex.ja: 英国人は概して保守的な国民である。

ex.en: The Conservative Party won the election in 1992.
ex.ja: １９９２年の選挙では保守党が勝利を収めた。

note.ja: con（共に・完全に）+ serv（保つ）+ ative。そのまま保とうとする →「保守的な」。conserve（保存する）も同じ。

en: To want; to wish for earnestly.
To put a request to (someone); to entreat.
The feeling of desiring; an eager longing for something.
Someone or something wished for.

desire.ety: From Middle English desir, desire (noun) and desiren (verb), from Old French desirer, desirrer, from Latin dēsīderō (“to long for, desire, feel the want of, miss, regret”), apparently from de- + sidus (in the phrase de sidere, "from the stars") in connection with astrological hopes. Compare consider and desiderate. The verb, along with Old Norse derived want (verb), has mostly replaced native will in modern English.

ex.en: I haven't had the desire for stuff lately.
ex.ja: 最近、物欲がわかなくてね。

ex.en: He has a burning desire to become famous.
ex.ja: 彼は有名になりたいと熱望している。

ex.en: There are no people who don't desire peace.
ex.ja: 平和を望まないものはいない。

note.ja: ラテン語 desiderare（星を待ち望む）から。de + sidus（星）。「星から運命を待つ」→「強く望む」。consider と同じ sider。

en: To damage beyond use or repair; to damage (something) to the point that it effectively ceases to exist.
To neutralize, undo a property or condition.

destroy.ety: From Middle English destroyen, from Old French destruire, Vulgar Latin *destrugō, from Classical Latin dēstruō, from dē- (“un-, de-”) + struō (“to build”).

ex.en: The soldiers' mission was to destroy the bridge.
ex.ja: 兵士たちの使命はその橋を破壊することだった。

ex.en: The accident destroyed all his hopes for success.
ex.ja: 思いがけない事故で彼の成功への夢は打ち砕かれてしまった。

ex.en: We think nuclear weapons will destroy our earth.
ex.ja: 核兵器はわが地球を滅ぼすと思う。

note.ja: de（逆に）+ stroy（積む）。積み上げたものを崩す →「破壊する」。construct（組み立てる）の反対。

en: A current of air, usually coming into a room or vehicle.
The draw through a flue of gasses or smoke resulting from a combustion process.
To write a first version; to make a preliminary sketch.
To draw in outline; to make a draught, sketch, or plan of, as in architectural and mechanical drawing.
Referring to drinks on tap, in contrast to bottled.
Referring to animals used for pulling heavy loads.

draft.ety: A phonetic spelling of draught (compare laughter), from Middle English draught, draght (“that which is pulled; that which is drawn up, a design”), from Old English *dreaht, *dræht, from Proto-West Germanic *drahti, *drahtu, from Proto-Germanic *drahtuz (“a pulling, drawing”). Cognate with Dutch dracht, German Tracht, Icelandic dráttur. By surface analysis, draw + -t.

ex.en: Thank you for the draft of the Agreement.
ex.ja: 契約書のドラフトをありがとうございました。

ex.en: I am writing a draft of the speech.
ex.ja: 私はスピーチの下書きを書いています。

ex.en: He is busy with the final draft.
ex.ja: 彼は最終稿に忙しく取り組んでいる。

en: Necessary.
Very important; of high importance.
A necessary ingredient.
A fundamental ingredient.

essential.ety: From Late Latin essentiālis, from Latin essentia (“being, essence”).

ex.en: It's essential for you to practice every day.
ex.ja: 毎日練習することが極めて重要です。

ex.en: A carry-on bag is essential for travel.
ex.ja: キャリーバッグは旅行に必須。

ex.en: Hard work is an essential element of success.
ex.ja: 努力は成功の基本要素である。

note.ja: essence（本質）+ -ial。ラテン語 esse（ある）。「本質的な」→「不可欠な」。

en: Known to one, or generally known; commonplace.
Acquainted.
An attendant spirit, often in animal or demon form.
A member of a pope's or bishop's household.

familiar.ety: From Middle English familiar, familier, from Latin familiāris (“pertaining to servants; pertaining to the household”). By surface analysis, family + -ar. Piecewise doublet of familial. Displaced native Old English hīwcūþ.

ex.en: I'm familiar with the way he asks questions.
ex.ja: 私は彼の質問の仕方を知っている。

ex.en: I am familiar with this part of town.
ex.ja: 私は町のこのあたりはよく知っている。

ex.en: Are you familiar with the rules of soccer?
ex.ja: あなたはサッカーのルールを知っていますか。

en: Responsible for a dishonest act.
Judged to have committed a crime.
A plea by a defendant who does not contest a charge.
A verdict of a judge or jury on a defendant judged to have committed a crime.

guilty.ety: From Middle English gilty, gulty, from Old English gyltiġ (“offending, guilty”); equivalent to guilt + -y.

ex.en: It cannot be denied that he is guilty.
ex.ja: 彼が有罪であることは否定できない。

ex.en: He refused to believe that she was guilty.
ex.ja: 彼女の有罪を彼は信じようとはしなかった。

ex.en: There's no need for you to feel guilty.
ex.ja: 君が罪悪感を抱く必要はないよ。

note.ja: guilt（罪）+ -y。古英語 gylt。「有罪の・罪悪感のある」。

en: Following the religion of Judaism.
Of or relating to Jews, their ethnicities or cultures.
A Jew.

Jewish.ety: From Jew + -ish. Compare Middle English Judewissh (“Jewish”), Old English Iūdēisċ (“Jewish”), Dutch joodsch, joods (“Jewish”), German jüdisch (“Jewish”), Danish jødisk (“Jewish”), Swedish judisk (“Jewish”), Gothic 𐌾𐌿𐌳𐌰𐌹𐍅𐌹𐍃𐌺𐍃 (judaiwisks, “Jewish”). See also the piecewise doublet Yiddish.

ex.en: "I don't drink wine." "Are you Jewish?" "No. I'm Muslim."
ex.ja: 「ワインは飲みません」「ユダヤ教なんですか？」「違いますよ。ムスリムです」

ex.en: "I don't drink wine." "Are you Jewish?" "No, I'm Muslim."
ex.ja: 「ワインは飲みません」「ユダヤ教なんですか？」「違いますよ。ムスリムです」

ex.en: Isaac was a leader of the Jewish people.
ex.ja: イサクはユダヤ人の指導者であった。

note.ja: Jew + -ish。Jew はヘブライ語 Yehudah（ユダ）から。

en: In a widespread or large manner.
For the most part; mainly or chiefly.

ex.ja: 彼の成功は大部分幸運によるものだった。

ex.ja: 私の成功はおもにあなたの助力のおかげだ。

ex.en: My success was largely due to luck.
ex.ja: 私の成功はもっぱら幸運の賜物だ。

note.ja: large（大きい）+ -ly。「大部分は・主に」。

en: With perfection.
Wholly, completely, totally.

perfectly.ety:

English perfect
Proto-Indo-European *leyg-der.

ex.ja: 君のことは充分理解しているつもりだよ。

ex.en: Few people can speak a foreign language perfectly.
ex.ja: 外国語を完璧に話せる人はほとんどいない。

ex.en: Tom learned French perfectly studying by himself.
ex.ja: トムは独学でフランス語をマスターした。

note.ja: perfect（完全な）+ -ly。per（完全に）+ facere（作る）。「作り上げられた」→「完全に」。

en: To bestow commendation on; to represent favorably; to suggest, endorse or encourage as an appropriate choice.
To make acceptable; to attract favor to.
A recommendation.

recommend.ety:
From Middle English recommenden, from Old French recommender (compare French recommander), from Latin re- + commendāre (“to commend, commit; to recommend”), from con- + mandāre (“commit, intrust, enjoin”), from manus (“hand, handwriting, power”) + dare (“to give; to offer or render”).

ex.en: He will recommend you for a good post.
ex.ja: 彼はあなたをよい地位に推薦するだろう。

ex.en: Tom is the one who recommended this book.
ex.ja: この本を薦めてくれたのはトムだ。

ex.en: Could you recommend a nice restaurant near here?
ex.ja: この近くのおいしいレストランを教えて下さい。

note.ja: re（強く）+ com + mend（委ねる）。強く委ねる →「推薦する・勧める」。

en: To direct the attention of (someone toward something).
To submit to (another person or group) for consideration; to send or direct elsewhere.
A blurb on the front page of a newspaper issue or section that refers the reader to the full story inside the issue or section by listing…

refer.ety: From Middle English referren, from Old French referer, from Latin referre. The noun (used in journalism) is from the verb. Doublet of relate. See also infer, collate and confer, delate and defer, as well as prelate and prefer among others.

ex.en: I often hear her refer to her childhood.
ex.ja: 彼女が子供の頃のことを言うのをよく耳にする。

ex.en: Her name was referred to in the meeting.
ex.ja: 彼女の名前が会議で出た。

ex.en: He even referred to the origin of life.
ex.ja: 彼は生命の起源にまで説き及んだ。

note.ja: re（元へ）+ fer（運ぶ）。（話や注意を）元へ運ぶ →「言及する・参照する・委ねる」。reference（参照）。

en: Related, connected, or pertinent to a topic.
Directly related, connected, or pertinent, with important ramifications or implications.

relevant.ety: From Scots relevant meaning "legally pertinent," used in Scottish legal circles starting in the early 1500s, and first used in English in the 1700s. Borrowed from Latin relevāns, relevāntem, present active participle of relevō (“lift up again, lighten, relieve”), from re- (“again”) + levō (“lift”).

ex.en: Your question is not relevant to the subject.
ex.ja: 君の質問は当面の話題とは関係がない。

ex.ja: 君の質問は当面の話題とは関係がない。

ex.ja: それはあんま関係ないと思う。

en: To try to find; to look for; to search for.
To try to acquire or gain; to strive after.
The operation of navigating through a stream.

seek.ety:
From Middle English seke, seken, from Old English sēċan, sēċean, sœ̄ċan, from Proto-West Germanic *sōkijan, from Proto-Germanic *sōkijaną (“to seek”), from Proto-Indo-European *séh₂gyeti (“to seek out”), from *seh₂g- (“to follow, trace”).

ex.en: We sought to come to terms with them.
ex.ja: われわれは彼らと妥協しようとした。

ex.en: Tom and Mary played hide-and-go-seek.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーはかくれんぼをしました。

ex.en: And they would play hide and go seek.
ex.ja: そして、彼らは、かくれんぼをしてあそんだ。

note.ja: 古英語 sēcan から。sake と同系。「探し求める」。

en: A piece of music for one performer.
A job or performance done by one person alone.
Without a companion or instructor.
Of, or relating to, a musical solo.
Alone, without a companion.
To perform a solo.
To perform something in the absence of anyone else.

solo.ety: Borrowed from Italian solo, from Latin sōlus, probably related to se (“himself”).

ex.en: I plan to play a flute solo.
ex.ja: フルート独奏をやるつもりです。

ex.en: The concert began with a piano solo.
ex.ja: 演奏会はピアノ独奏から始まった。

ex.en: Nancy set out on a solo journey.
ex.ja: ナンシーは一人で旅に出た。

note.ja: イタリア語 solo（ひとりの）から。ラテン語 solus と同じ。→「独奏・単独で」。

en: A pass entitling the holder to admission to a show, concert, sporting event, etc.
A pass entitling the holder to board a train, a bus, a plane, or other means of transportation.
To issue someone a ticket, as for travel or for a violation of a local or traffic law.
To mark with a ticket.

ex.ja: 今日はチケットが手に入るかどうか分からない。

ex.ja: 私は彼らにチケットをもう一枚送ってくれるように頼んだ。

ex.ja: トムはメアリーにチケットを買うお金を渡した。

en: Not able; lacking a certain ability.
Indicating that a requested course of action is not possible to carry out.

unable.ety: From Middle English unable, unabel, unhable, unhabil, equivalent to un- + able.

ex.en: I am unable to agree on that point.
ex.ja: その点は賛成しかねる。

ex.en: He is unable to provide for his family.
ex.ja: 彼は自分の家族を養う事ができない。

ex.en: Tom was unable to do that by himself.
ex.ja: トムはそれを一人ではできなかった。

en: Angry, distressed, or unhappy
Feeling unwell, nauseated, or ready to vomit.
Disturbance or disruption.
An unexpected victory of a competitor or candidate that was not favored to win.
To make (a person) angry, distressed, or unhappy.
To disturb, disrupt or adversely alter (something).

upset.ety: From Middle English upset (“the act of setting up; establishment”), from Middle English upsetten, corresponding to up- + set. Cognate with Middle Low German upset (“setup; arrangement”).

ex.en: She looked upset as she read the letter.
ex.ja: 彼女はその手紙を読んでいる時うろたえた様子だった。

ex.en: I can't understand why Tom is so upset.
ex.ja: トムが何であんなに怒るのか理解できない。

ex.en: I hope you don't get an upset stomach.
ex.ja: 気持ち悪くならないといいね。

en: An appendage of an animal's (bird, bat, insect) body that enables it to fly.
A fin at the side of a ray or similar fish.
To injure slightly (as with a gunshot), especially in the wing or arm.
To fly.

wing.ety:
From Middle English winge, wenge, from Old Norse vængr ("wing of a flying animal, wing of a building"; compare vængi (“ship's cabin”)), from Proto-Germanic *wēingijaz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂weh₁- (“to blow”), thus related to wind.
Cognate with Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, and Swedish vinge (“wing”), Elfdalian waingg (“wing”), Faroese vongur (“wing”), Icelandic vængur (“wing”), Norwegian Nynorsk veng (“wing”).
Replaced native Middle English fither (from Old English fiþre, from Proto-Germanic *fiþriją), which merged with Middle English fether (from Old English feþer, from Proto-Germanic *feþr

ex.en: I love the chicken wings from that restaurant.
ex.ja: あのお店の手羽先が大好きなの。

ex.en: I wish I had wings to fly.
ex.ja: 私に空を飛ぶ翼があったらいいのになあ。

ex.en: The reason is they immediately wing it.
ex.ja: すぐ知ったかぶりをするんだから。

note.ja: 古北欧語 vængr から。「翼」→ 建物の「棟」→ 政党の左右の「派」。

en: An explosive device used or intended as a weapon, especially, one dropped from an aircraft.
Events or conditions that have a speedy destructive effect.
To attack using one or more bombs; to bombard.
To attack or annoy in the manner of a bombing.

ex.ja: 選挙運動は実に順調にいっているようだ。

ex.ja: 爆撃にでもあったかのような部屋ね。

en: Tending to create things, or having the ability to create; often, excellently, in a novel fashion, or any or all of these.
Original, expressive and imaginative.
A person directly involved in a creative process; a creator of creative content.
Artistic material used in advertising, e.g. photographs, drawings, or videos.

ex.ja: これは私達自信の創造活動の所産です。

ex.en: Tom is a very creative person.
ex.ja: トムはとても創造性のある人だ。

note.ja: create（創造する）+ -ive。ラテン語 creare。「創造的な」。

en: An interval of space or time in which one set of events or phenomena is completed.
A complete rotation of anything.
To go through a cycle or to put through a cycle.
To turn power off and back on

cycle.ety:
From Middle English cicle (“fixed length period of years”), from Late Latin cyclus, from Ancient Greek κύκλος (kúklos, “circle”), from Proto-Hellenic *kúklos, *kʷókʷlos, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷékʷlos (“circle, wheel”).
Doublet of chakra, chakram, charkha, chukker, cyclus, kike, and wheel (see there for more).

ex.en: We're going to cycle to the lake tomorrow.
ex.ja: 私たちはあす湖まで自転車で行きます。

ex.en: We are going to cycle to the lake tomorrow.
ex.ja: 私たちはあす湖まで自転車で行きます。

ex.en: The cycle of blood is not regular.
ex.ja: 血液の循環。

Instructive, or helping to educate.
A free (or low cost) trip for travel consultants, provided by a travel operator or airline as a means of promoting their service. A fam trip
An educational seminar, workshop, etc.

ex.ja: 彼は教育制度の改革を提案した。

ex.ja: 給料は、経験と学歴に基づいて決まります。

ja: エンターテインメント

en: An activity designed to give pleasure, enjoyment, diversion, amusement, or relaxation to an audience, no matter whether the audience part…
A show put on for the enjoyment or amusement of others.

entertainment.ety: From Middle English entretenement (“support, maintenance”), from Old French entretenement; see entertain. Morphologically entertain + -ment.

ex.en: There's no entertainment for young people around here.
ex.ja: ここいらの若者には娯楽がない。

ex.en: Entertainment is still popular with young people in Japan.
ex.ja: エンターテインメントは、日本でもやっぱり若者に人気がある。

ex.en: This event offers various items of entertainment.
ex.ja: このイベントは様々なエンターテイメントを提供しています。

note.ja: entertain（もてなす）+ -ment。inter（間）+ tenere（保つ）。「間を持たせる」→「もてなし・娯楽」。maintain と同じ ten。

en: Of a place, the most remote, farthest or outermost.
In the greatest or highest degree; intense.
The greatest or utmost point, degree, or condition.
Each of the things at opposite ends of a range or scale.

extreme.ety: Borrowed into late Middle English from Old French extreme, from Latin extrēmus, the superlative of exter.

ex.en: She is extreme in her taste in clothes.
ex.ja: 彼女は洋服の好みが極端だ。

ex.en: His way of thinking is a bit extreme.
ex.ja: 彼の考え方は少し極端だ。

ex.en: I hear you've done some pretty extreme stuff.
ex.ja: かなりあくどい事をしてきたそうだな。

en: To be or remain suspended.
To float, as if suspended.
The way in which something hangs.
A mass of hanging material.

hang.ety:
From Middle English hangen, hongen, from a fusion of Old English hōn (“to hang, be hanging”, transitive verb) and hangian (“to hang, cause to hang”, intransitive verb), respectively from the transitive verb Proto-West Germanic *hą̄han and the intransitive verb *hangēn; also probably influenced by Old Norse hengja (“to suspend”) and hanga (“to be suspended”); all from Proto-Germanic *hanhaną and *hangāną, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱenk- (“to waver, be in suspense”).
See also Dutch hangen, Low German hangen and hängen, German hängen, Norwegian Bokmål henge, Norwegian Nynorsk henga; also Gothic 𐌷

ex.en: A strange person is hanging around the house.
ex.ja: 変な人が家の周りをうろついてるわよ。

ex.en: I'm getting the hang of this new machine.
ex.ja: この新しい機械の使い方がわかりかけてきたところです。

ex.en: The hot sun made the flowers hang down.
ex.ja: 暑さのために花は萎れた。

en: Of a person or thing being the driving force influencing the outcome of an event; chiefly; certainly for the most part.

mainly.ety: From Middle English maynly; equivalent to main + -ly.

ex.en: The Japanese used to live mainly on rice.
ex.ja: 日本人は以前は主に米を主食としていた。

ex.en: My success was mainly due to your help.
ex.ja: 私が成功したのは主にあなたの援助のためであった。

ex.en: The party is mainly made up of working women.
ex.ja: その党は主に働く女性から成り立っている。

note.ja: main（主な）+ -ly。古英語 mægen（力）。「主に」。

en: The highest limit.
The greatest value of a set or other mathematical structure, especially the global maximum or a local maximum of a function.
To the highest degree.

ex.en: I got 80 marks out of a maximum of 100.
ex.ja: 私は１００点満点で８０点取った。

ex.en: You may spend a maximum of 100 dollars.
ex.ja: 最高百ドルまで遣ってよい。

ex.en: This hall holds a maximum of 1,000 people.
ex.ja: このホールは最大で１０００人収容できる。

note.ja: ラテン語 maximum（最大のもの）から。maximus（最も大きい）。minimum の対。magnus と同じ語根。

en: A publication, usually published daily or weekly, containing news and other articles. Traditionally a print publication typically printed…
The news organization that produces such a publication.
To cover with newspaper.
To engage in the business of journalism

ex.en: Are you able to read a French newspaper?
ex.ja: フランス語の新聞って読める？

ex.en: I read the newspaper to keep myself informed.
ex.ja: 世間を知るように新聞を読んでいます。

ex.en: At school I am on the Newspaper Committee.
ex.ja: 学校では新聞委員会に入っています。

note.ja: news（ニュース）+ paper（紙）。「新聞」。

en: A substance that is applied as a liquid or paste, and dries into a solid coating that protects or adds colour to an object or surface to …
A set of containers or blocks of paint of different colors/colours, used for painting pictures.
To apply paint to.
To apply in the manner that paint is applied.

ex.en: I like the picture painted in water colors.
ex.ja: 私は水彩画が好きです。

ex.ja: その家は父によってペンキが塗られていた。

ex.ja: その家は職人の手でペンキを塗られている。

en: A state where sovereignty rests with the people or their representatives, rather than with a monarch or emperor; a country with no monarchy.
One of the subdivisions constituting Russia. See oblast.

ex.en: He immediately started the next attack on the republic.
ex.ja: 彼はすかさず共和国への次の攻撃を開始した。

ex.en: Tom was elected President of the Republic.
ex.ja: トムは共和国の大統領に選ばれたんだ。

ex.en: After the revolution, France became a republic.
ex.ja: 革命後、フランスは共和国になった。

note.ja: re（= res 事柄）+ publ（人々の）+ ic。ラテン語 res publica（人々の事柄）から →「共和国」。

en: The act of reserving or keeping back; reservation; exception.
Restraint of freedom in words or actions; backwardness; caution in personal behavior.
To keep back; to retain.
To keep in store for future or special use.

reserve.ety: From Old French reserver, from Latin reservō (“to reserve, retain”).

ex.en: I'd like to reserve a table for three.
ex.ja: わたしは３人でテーブルを予約したい。

ex.en: I'd like to reserve a table for two.
ex.ja: ２人分の席を予約したいのですが。

ex.en: Did you reserve a room at the hotel?
ex.ja: ホテルの部屋を予約しましたか。

note.ja: re（後ろに）+ serv（保つ）。後ろに取っておく →「予約する・蓄え」。

Specifically, a line of buildings on a street; also, the street itself (especially in street names)
To propel (a boat or other craft) over water using oars.
To transport in a boat propelled with oars.

ex.en: I noticed that she sat in the front row.
ex.ja: 彼女が前の列に座っているのに気づいた。

ex.en: The student missed class three times in a row.
ex.ja: その生徒は三回続けて授業に出なかった。

ex.en: Yes! I won twice in a row!
ex.ja: やった！2回続けて勝っちゃった！

en: A common substance, chemically consisting mainly of sodium chloride (NaCl), used extensively as a food ingredient, seasoning, condiment, …
One of the compounds formed from the reaction of an acid with a base, where a positive ion replaces a hydrogen of the acid.
Of water: containing salt, saline.
Treated with salt as a preservative; cured with salt, salted.
To add salt to.
To deposit salt as a saline solution.

salt.ety:

From Middle English salt, from Old English sealt, from Proto-West Germanic *salt, from Proto-Germanic *saltą, from Proto-Indo-European *sḗh₂l (“salt”). Doublet of sal, salary, and salsa, all ultimately from Latin sāl (“salt”), which it superseded as the general term for "salt".
Cognate with Dutch zout, German Salz, Danish, Faroese, Icelandic, Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, and Swedish salt.

ex.en: She asked me to pass her the salt.
ex.ja: 彼女は私に塩を取ってくれるように頼んだ。

ex.en: He asked me to pass him the salt.
ex.ja: 塩を回してください、と彼は私に言った。

ex.en: She put salt into her coffee by mistake.
ex.ja: 彼女は間違ってコーヒーに塩を入れた。

note.ja: 古英語 sealt から。ラテン語 sal（salary、salad）と同じ祖先。

en: A minor fright.
A cause of terror or alarm; a panic; something that inspires fear or dread.
To frighten, terrify, startle, especially in a minor way.
(To be able) to be scared.
lean; scanty

scare.ety: From Middle English sker, skere (“terror, fright”), from the verb Middle English skerren (“to frighten”) (see below).

ex.en: A loud noise in the night scared him.
ex.ja: 夜の大きな音で彼はおびえた。

ex.en: My little sister is scared of all doctors.
ex.ja: 妹はどんな医者も怖がる。

ex.en: She was so scared that she couldn't speak.
ex.ja: 彼女は余りにもおびえて口がきけなかった。

en: A single item in a statistical study.
A quantity calculated from the data in a sample, which characterises an important aspect in the sample (such as mean or standard deviation).
To analyze or describe using statistics.
To cite or calculate statistics.

ex.en: Statistics deals with collected numbers representing facts.
ex.ja: 統計学は事実を表す数を取り扱うものである。

ex.en: According to statistics, world population is on the rise.
ex.ja: 統計によれば世界の人口は増加している。

ex.en: Statistics don't always tell the whole story.
ex.ja: 統計はすべてを物語るとは限らない。

en: A device to turn electric current on and off or direct its flow.
A change or exchange.
To exchange.
To change (something) to the specified state using a switch.
Pertaining to riding with the front and back feet swapped round compared to one's normal position.
Pertaining to skiing backwards.

switch.ety: Perhaps from Middle Dutch swijch (“twig”), first attested in c. 1592. The mechanical device for altering the direction of something sense is first attested in c. 1797, pertaining to pivoted rails on minecart railways, which were once wooden.

ex.en: Switch on the light. I can't see anything.
ex.ja: 電灯を点けてくれ。何も見えないよ。

ex.en: I felt for the switch in the dark.
ex.ja: 僕は暗闇の中でスイッチを手探りでさがした。

ex.en: On no account must you touch that switch.
ex.ja: 絶対にそのスイッチに触れてはいけない。

en: A large extent or tract of land; for example a region, country or district.
One of three of Canada's federal entities, located in the country's Arctic, with fewer powers than a province and created by an act of Pa…

territory.ety: Inherited from Middle English territorie, from Latin territōrium.

ex.en: They controlled a fifth part of the territory.
ex.ja: 彼らは領土の５分の１を支配していた。

ex.en: They increased the territory of the empire.
ex.ja: 彼らは帝国の領土を広げた。

ex.en: Japan claims the Northern Territories for its own.
ex.ja: 日本は北方領土を日本固有のものにしたがっている。

note.ja: ラテン語 territorium（町の周りの土地）から。terra（土地）。「領土」。terrain、Mediterranean と同じ。

en: An expression of intent to injure or punish another.
An indication of potential or imminent danger.
To press; urge; compel.
To use threats; act or speak menacingly; threaten.

threat.ety: From Middle English threte, thret, thrat, thræt, threat, from Old English þrēat (“crowd, swarm, troop, army, press; pressure, trouble, calamity, oppression, force, violence, threat”), from Proto-Germanic *þrautaz, closely tied to Proto-Germanic *þrautą (“displeasure, complaint, grievance, labour, toil”), from Proto-Indo-European *trewd- (“to squeeze, push, press”). Cognate with Scots thret, threte, threit (“threat”), Middle High German drōz (“annoyance, disgust, horror, terror, fright”), Middle Low German drōt (“threat, menace, danger”), Faroese treyt (“struggle, labour, distress”), Icelandic

ex.en: His threat got me to start studying seriously.
ex.ja: 彼が脅したので私は本気で勉強をするはめになった。

ex.en: We thought his threat was only a joke.
ex.ja: 彼の脅しは単なる冗談かと思った。

ex.en: Don't worry about Tom. He isn't a threat.
ex.ja: トムのことは気にする必要はない。彼は危険な存在じゃない。

note.ja: 古英語 thrēat（圧迫・群衆）から。「押しつけること」→「脅し・脅威」。threaten。

en: To set, fix or determine (a time or place for something such as a meeting, or the meeting itself) by authority or agreement.
To name (someone to a post or role).

appoint.ety: From Middle English apointen, borrowed from Old French apointier (“to prepare, arrange, lean, place”) (French appointer (“to give a salary, refer a cause”)), from Late Latin appunctō (“to bring back to the point, restore, to fix the point in a controversy, or the points in an agreement”); Latin ad + punctum (“a point”). See point.

ex.en: She came an hour beyond the appointed time.
ex.ja: 彼女は約束の時間を１時間過ぎて来た。

ex.en: The president appointed each man to the post.
ex.ja: 大統領はそれぞれをその地位に任命した。

ex.en: He appointed John to act as his deputy.
ex.ja: 彼はジョンにかわりを務めるように命じた。

note.ja: ap（〜へ）+ point（点）。ある点に定める →「任命する・（日時を）指定する」。appointment（約束・任命）。

en: To or on one side so as to be out of the way.
Excluded from consideration.
Not in perfect symmetry; distorted laterally, especially of the human body.
An incidental remark to a person next to one made discreetly but not in private, audible only to that person.
A brief comment by a character addressing the audience, unheard by other characters.

aside.ety: From Middle English aside, asyde, a-side, oside, from Middle English on side, from Old English on sīdan (literally “on (the) side (of)”), equivalent to a- + side. Compare beside.

ex.en: Aside from this, he was in good health.
ex.ja: このことを除けば、彼は健康であった。

ex.en: He puts aside a little money each month.
ex.ja: 彼は毎月少しずつお金を貯めている。

ex.en: He laid aside a few dollars each week.
ex.ja: 彼は毎週何ドルかずつ貯めておいた。

note.ja: a（〜に）+ side（そば）。「わきに」→「別にして」。

en: Aid; help; the act or result of assisting.

assistance.ety: From Middle English assistance, from Middle French assistance, from Medieval Latin assistentia, from Latin assistō (“to stand at”). By surface analysis, assist + -ance.

ex.en: Call on me if you need my assistance.
ex.ja: 助けが必要だったら呼んでくれ。

ex.en: I can't thank you enough for your assistance.
ex.ja: ご助力に対してはお礼の申しようもありません。

ex.en: It was a mistake to refuse his assistance.
ex.ja: 彼の助力を断ったのは間違いだ。

note.ja: assist（助ける）+ -ance。ad + sistere（立つ）。「そばに立つ」→「手助け」。consist、insist と同じ。

en: A percussive instrument made of metal or other hard material, typically but not always in the shape of an inverted cup with a flared rim,…
An instrument that emits a ringing sound, situated on a bicycle's handlebar and used by the cyclist to warn of their presence.
To attach a bell to.
To shape so that it flares out like a bell.

ex.en: The question is: Who will bell the cat.
ex.ja: 問題は誰が猫に鈴をつけるかだ。

ex.en: The church bell used to ring at three.
ex.ja: 教会の鐘は３時に鳴ったものです。

ex.en: Who can put a bell on the cat?
ex.ja: だれがその猫に鈴をつけられるか。

note.ja: 古英語 belle から。bellow（ほえる）と同系とされる。

en: To produce an air current.
To propel by an air current (or, if under water, a water current), usually with the mouth.
A strong wind.
A chance to catch one's breath.
Used to express displeasure or frustration.
Blue.

From Middle English blowen, from Old English blāwan (“to blow, breathe, inflate, sound”), from Proto-West Germanic *blāan, from Proto-Germanic *blēaną (“to blow”) (compare German blähen), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰleh₁- (“to swell, blow up”) (compare Latin flō (“to blow”) and Old Armenian բեղուն (bełun, “fertile”)).

ex.en: A blow from a falling stone killed him.
ex.ja: 彼は落石で即死した。

ex.en: I had a mental blow at that time.
ex.ja: 私はそのとき精神的なショックを受けた。

ex.en: Her death is a blow to my feelings.
ex.ja: 彼女の死はぼくの気持ちには打撃です。

en: A document constituting evidence of a long-term debt, by which the bond issuer (the borrower) is obliged to pay interest when due, and re…
A documentary obligation to pay a sum or to perform a contract; a debenture.
To connect, secure or tie with a bond; to bind.
To cause to adhere (one material with another).
Subject to the tenure called bondage.
In a state of servitude or slavedom; not free.

bond.ety: From Middle English bond, a variant of band, from Old English beand, bænd, bend (“bond, chain, fetter, band, ribbon, ornament, chaplet, crown”), from Proto-Germanic *bandaz, *bandiz (“band, fetter”)، from Proto-Indo-European *bʰendʰ- (“to tie; bond, band”). Cognate with Dutch band, German Band, Swedish band. Doublet of Bund. Related to bind.

ex.en: There is a strong bond between the brothers.
ex.ja: その兄弟の間には強い絆がある。

ex.en: At last, James Bond made it as an actor.
ex.ja: やっとジェームズ・ボンドは俳優として成功した。

ex.en: Currency and bond markets are relatively calm.
ex.ja: 通貨市場、債券市場は比較的落ち着いている。

en: A male partner in an unmarried romantic relationship.
A male friend.

From boy + friend.

ex.en: I am not gay, but my boyfriend is.
ex.ja: 私はゲイじゃないけど、私の彼はゲイだよ。

ex.en: I'm going to Germany to visit my boyfriend.
ex.ja: 彼氏に会いに、ドイツに行きます。

ex.en: Tom is just a friend, not my boyfriend.
ex.ja: トムはただの友達で、彼氏じゃないよ。

en: Taking care; attentive to potential danger, error or harm; cautious.
Conscientious and painstaking; meticulous.

careful.ety: From Middle English careful, from Old English carful; equivalent to care + -ful.

ex.en: I'll be careful never to be late again.
ex.ja: 二度と遅刻しないように気をつけます。

ex.en: I am not more careful than you are.
ex.ja: 私は君ほど注意深くない。

ex.en: You cannot be too careful of your health.
ex.ja: どんなに健康に注意してもしすぎることはない。

en: Something which is related to, or in some way affects, a fact or event.
An event; a fact; a particular incident, occurrence, or condition (status).
To place in a particular situation, especially with regard to money or other resources.

ex.en: I ended up seeing it under bad circumstances.
ex.ja: 私はまずい状況でそれを見ることになってしまった。

ex.en: Circumstances forced us to put off the meeting.
ex.ja: 我々はやむを得ない事情で、その会合を延期した。

ex.en: Under these circumstances, I cannot accept the offer.
ex.ja: こういう事情なので、私はその申し出を受け取ることはできない。

note.ja: circum（周りに）+ stan（立つ）+ ce。周りに立っているもの →「状況・事情」。

en: A body corporate, created by law or under authority of law, having a continuous existence independent of the existences of its members, a…
The municipal governing body of a borough or city.

corporation.ety:
From Middle English corporacion, corporation, from Late Latin corporatio (“assumption of a body”), from Latin corporatus, past participle of corporare (“to form into a body”); see corporate. By surface analysis, corporate + -ion.
(protruding belly): Perhaps a play on the word corpulence.

ex.en: The two companies combined in a joint corporation.
ex.ja: その二つの会社は合併して合弁会社となった。

ex.en: She works for a large American corporation.
ex.ja: 彼女はアメリカの大会社に勤めている。

ex.en: My father holds the major interest in the corporation.
ex.ja: 父はその会社の過半数の株を所有している。

note.ja: ラテン語 corpus（体）から。corp + or + ation。一つの体としてまとまった団体 →「法人・企業」。

en: To shed tears; to weep, especially in anger or sadness.
To utter loudly; to call out; to declare publicly.
A shedding of tears; the act of crying.
A shout or scream.

cry.ety:
The verb is from Middle English crien (13th century), from Old French crier, from Vulgar Latin *crītāre, generally thought to derive from Classical Latin quirītāre (Proto-West Germanic *krītan has also been suggested as a source). The noun corresponds to Middle English cry, crie, from Old French cri, a deverbal of crier.
etymology note
Middle English crien eventually displaced native Middle English galen (“to cry out”) (from Old English galan), Middle English greden (“to cry out”) (from Old English grǣdan), Middle English yermen (“to bellow, mourn, lament”) (from Old English ġierman), Middle E

ex.en: I'm sorry that I made you cry yesterday.
ex.ja: 昨日は泣かせてごめん。

ex.en: When I see that play, I always cry.
ex.ja: あの芝居を見ると必ず涙が出てくる。

ex.en: No one can read the book without crying.
ex.ja: その本を読むと誰でも泣かずにはいられない。

note.ja: 古フランス語 crier（叫ぶ）から。ラテン語 quiritare（市民に助けを求めて叫ぶ）。「叫ぶ」→「泣く」。

en: Exposure to likely harm; risk of death or serious injury.
An instance or cause of likely serious harm.

danger.ety: From Middle English daunger (“power, dominion, peril”), from Anglo-Norman dangier, from Old French dangier, alteration of Old French dongier (due to association with Latin damnum (“damage”)) from Vulgar Latin *dominiārium (“authority, power”) from Latin dominus (“lord, master”). Displaced native Old English frēcennes.

ex.en: He stood firm in the face of danger.
ex.ja: 彼は危険に直面しても動じなかった。

ex.en: He was calm in the presence of danger.
ex.ja: 彼は危険に直面しても冷静だった。

ex.en: I was in danger of losing my life.
ex.ja: 私は生命を失う危険にさらされていた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 dangier（支配権）から。ラテン語 dominium。「他人に支配される状態」→「危険」。dominate と同系。

en: The act of conveying something.
The item which has been conveyed.

delivery.ety: From Middle English deliveri et al., from Anglo-Norman, from Old French delivrer.

ex.en: The pizza delivery guy hasn't come by yet.
ex.ja: ピザの宅配の人、まだ来ないのよ。

ex.en: The article will be sent cash on delivery.
ex.ja: 品物は代金引換でお送りいたします。

ex.en: The pizza delivery man hasn't come yet.
ex.ja: ピザの宅配の人、まだ来ないのよ。

note.ja: deliver（配達する）+ -y。de + liberare（自由にする）。「手放して渡す」→「配達・出産」。liberty と同じ。

en: To be entitled to, as a result of past actions; to be worthy to have.

deserve.ety: From Middle English deserven, from Old French deservir, from Latin dēserviō, from dē- + serviō.

ex.en: I know that I don't deserve you.
ex.ja: 僕があなたに見合わないのは分かっています。

ex.en: The honor is more than I deserve.
ex.ja: それは身に余る光栄でございます。

ex.en: I don't deserve to live.
ex.ja: 私には生きる価値がない。

note.ja: de（完全に）+ serv（仕える）。十分に仕えた →「〜に値する」。

en: Devoid of content; containing nothing or nobody; vacant.
Containing no elements (as of a string, array, or set), opposed to being null (having no valid value).
To make empty; to remove the contents of.
Of a river, duct, etc: to drain or flow toward an ultimate destination.
A container, especially a bottle, whose contents have been used up, leaving it empty.

empty.ety:
From Middle English emty, amty, from Old English ǣmtiġ, ǣmettiġ (“vacant, empty, free, idle, unmarried”, literally “without must or obligation, leisurely”), from Proto-Germanic *uz- (“out”) + Proto-Germanic *mōtijô, *mōtô (“must, obligation, need”), *mōtiþô (“ability, accommodation”), from Proto-Indo-European *med- (“measure; to acquire, possess, be in command”). Related to Old English ġeǣmtigian (“to empty”), ǣmetta (“leisure”), mōtan (“can, to be allowed”). More at mote, meet.
The interconsonantal excrescent p is a euphonic insertion dating from Middle English.

ex.en: The house was empty except for a cat.
ex.ja: １匹の猫を別とすれば家は空っぽだった。

ex.en: The box, which I had found was empty.
ex.ja: 見つけた箱には何もなかった。

ex.en: My life would be completely empty without you.
ex.ja: 君がいなければ私の人生は全くむなしいだろう。

note.ja: 古英語 ǣmettig（暇な）から。「何もない」→「空の」。

en: People, persons.
One’s relatives, especially one’s parents.
Of or pertaining to the inhabitants of a land, their culture, tradition, or history.
Of or pertaining to common people as opposed to ruling classes or elites.

folk.ety:

Proto-Germanic *fulką
Proto-West Germanic *folk
Old English folc
Middle English folk
English folk
From Middle English folk, from Old English folc, from Proto-West Germanic *folk, from Proto-Germanic *fulką, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *pl̥h₁-gós, from *pleh₁- (“to fill”).
Cognate with Saterland Frisian Foulk, West Frisian folk, Dutch volk, German Low German and German Volk, Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, and Swedish folk, Faroese and Icelandic fólk. Doublet of volk.

ex.en: Folks, it's time I was leaving.
ex.ja: 皆さん、私はもう行く時間です。

ex.en: Now folks, let's go on.
ex.ja: さあ、みんな、先へ進もう。

ex.en: I don't like all of these folk songs.
ex.ja: 私はこれらのフォークソングすべてが好きというわけではない。

en: Sex (a category, either male or female, into which sexually-reproducing organisms are divided on the basis of their reproductive roles in…
Identification as a man, a woman, or something else, and association with a (social) role or set of behavioral and cultural traits, cloth…
To assign a gender to (a person); to perceive as having a gender; to address using terms (pronouns, nouns, adjectives...) that express a …
To perceive (a thing) as having characteristics associated with a certain gender, or as having been authored by someone of a certain gender.
Evoking positive feelings regarding gender, like gender euphoria or gender envy.

gender.ety: From Middle English gendre, borrowed from Old French gendre, borrowed from Latin genere (“type, kind”). Doublet of genre and genus. The verb developed after the noun. Displaced native Old English hād (“sex, gender”).

ex.en: Tom believes in traditional gender roles.
ex.ja: トムは男尊女卑思想の持ち主だ。

ex.en: Equestrian is the only mixed-gender Olympic event.
ex.ja: 馬術競技は男女混合で行われる唯一のオリンピック競技です。

ex.en: We had a really interesting conversation whilst enjoying the mixed gender bath.
ex.ja: 混浴を楽しみながら会話に花をさかせました。

note.ja: ラテン語 genus（種類）から。gen（生まれ・種類）+ der。種類 →「（文法・社会的な）性」。

en: An occasion; an order of occurrence.
A case offered as an exemplification or a precedent; an illustrative example.
To mention as a case or example; to refer to.
To cite an example as proof; to exemplify.

instance.ety: Borrowed from Middle French instance, from Latin īnstantia (“a being near, presence, also perseverance, earnestness, importunity, urgency”), from īnstāns (“urgent”); see instant.

ex.en: This is an instance of modern British life.
ex.ja: これは英国の現代生活のほんの一例だ。

ex.en: Take, for instance, your family problems.
ex.ja: たとえばあなたの家庭のいざこざを考えてごらんなさい。

ex.en: I want to go abroad, for instance, to Italy and Spain.
ex.ja: 私は例えばイタリアやスペインなど外国へ行きたい。

note.ja: in（近くに）+ stan（立つ）+ ce。すぐそばに立っているもの →「実例・場合」。for instance は「例えば」。

en: A change whereby something goes from one place to another; a state of progression from one place to another; a change of position with re…
A parliamentary action to propose something. A similar procedure in any official or business meeting.
To gesture indicating a desired movement.
To introduce a motion in parliamentary procedure.

motion.ety: Inherited from Middle English mocioun, mocion, from Anglo-Norman motion, Middle French motion, and their etymon Latin mōtiō (“movement, motion”), related to movēre, from Proto-Indo-European *m(y)ewh₁- (“to move”).

ex.en: It was like watching a slow motion movie.
ex.ja: それはまるでスローモーション映画を見ているようだった。

ex.en: The scene was shown in slow motion.
ex.ja: その場面はスローモーションで再生された。

ex.en: When will this machine be put in motion again?
ex.ja: いつまたこの機械は動きはじめますか。

note.ja: mot（動く）+ ion。動くこと →「動き・動作・動議」。emotion（感情）、promotion（前へ動かす→昇進・販売促進）も同じ。

en: Calm, peaceful.
Preferring peace by nature; avoiding violence.

ex.en: Our plane was flying over the Pacific Ocean.
ex.ja: われわれの飛行機は太平洋の上を飛んで行った。

ex.en: He crossed the Pacific Ocean in thirty days.
ex.ja: 彼は三十日で太平洋を渡った。

ex.en: He was the first man to cross the Pacific.
ex.ja: 彼は最初に太平洋を渡った人だった。

en: That which is taken from another; something captured; a thing seized by force, stratagem, or superior power.
Anything captured by a belligerent using the rights of war; especially, property captured at sea in virtue of the rights of war, as a ves…
To consider highly valuable; to esteem.
To move with a lever; to force up or open; to prise or pry.
Having won a prize; award-winning.
First-rate; exceptional.

prize.ety: From Middle English prise, from Old French prise (“a taking, capture, a seizure, a thing seized, a prize, booty, also hold, purchase”), past participle of prendre (“to take, to capture”), from Latin prēndere (“to take, seize”); see prehend. Compare prison, apprise, comprise, enterprise, purprise, reprisal, surprise, etc. Doublet of prise.

ex.en: Never did I dream of winning first prize.
ex.ja: １等になるなんて夢にも思わなかった。

ex.en: I was surprised that you won the prize.
ex.ja: 君が入賞したのにはびっくりした。

ex.en: He is proud of having won the prize.
ex.ja: 彼はその賞をとったことを誇りに思っている。

note.ja: ラテン語 pretium（値段・価値）から。価値あるものとして与えられる →「賞・賞品」。price（値段）、precious（貴重な）も同語源。

en: Just; fair; agreeable to reason.
Not excessive or immoderate; within due limits; proper.

reasonable.ety: From Middle English resonable, from Old French resnable, from Classical Latin ratiōnābilis, from ratiō. By surface analysis, reason + -able. Doublet of rationable.

ex.en: The price of this used car is reasonable.
ex.ja: この中古車の価格は手ごろだ。

ex.en: A good management would listen to reasonable demands.
ex.ja: 良い経営陣なら正当な要求に耳を貸すものだ。

ex.en: I'll go tomorrow if the weather is reasonable.
ex.ja: 明日天気が良かったら行きます。

en: A formal recording of names, events, transactions, etc.
A book of such entries.
To enter in a register; to enlist.
To sign-up, especially to vote.

register.ety: From Medieval Latin registrum, from Late Latin regesta (“list, items recorded”), from Latin regerō (“to record, to carry back”), from re- + gerō (“to carry, bear”). Compare Latin registoria (“a treasurer”). Some senses influenced by association with unrelated Latin regō (“to rule”).

ex.en: New guests must register in the hotel book.
ex.ja: 新しい客はホテルの宿帳に登録せねばならない。

ex.en: Those two went to the register to pay.
ex.ja: 二人はレジへ行き精算した。

ex.en: The couple went to the register and paid.
ex.ja: 二人はレジへ行き精算した。

en: A firm decision or an official decision.
A strong will; the state of being resolute.

resolution.ety: Recorded since 1412, as Middle English resolucioun (“dissolution”), either from Anglo-Norman resolucion or directly from Latin resolūtiō (“a loosening, solution”), from resolvō (“to loosen”), itself from the intensive prefix re- + solvō (“to loosen”). By surface analysis, recognizably related to resolve and -tion.

ex.en: He made a firm resolution never to repeat it.
ex.ja: 彼は二度とそれを繰り返すまいとかたい決心をした。

ex.en: The resolution to the problem was close at hand.
ex.ja: その問題を解決するのはもうすぐだった。

ex.en: The resolution that a new road be built was passed.
ex.ja: 新しく道路を作るという決議が可決されました。

note.ja: re（強く）+ solu（解く）+ tion。強く解きほぐすこと →「解決・決意・決議・解像度」。resolve（解決する・決心する）。

en: Relating to the countryside or to agriculture.

rural.ety: From Old French rural, from Latin rūrālis (“rural”), from rūs (“countryside”) + -ālis.

ex.en: I want to live in a rural area.
ex.ja: 田舎に住みたいな。

ex.en: You will soon be used to rural life.
ex.ja: あなたはもうすぐ田舎の生活に慣れるでしょう。

ex.en: I want to live in rural areas.
ex.ja: 田舎に住みたいな。

note.ja: ラテン語 ruralis から。rus（田舎）。urban（都会の）の対。rustic と同じ。

en: To produce musical or harmonious sounds with one’s voice.
To perform a vocal part in a musical composition, regardless of technique.
The act, or event, of singing songs.
Any sound likened to human singing.

sing.ety: From Middle English syngen, from Old English singan (“to sing”), from Proto-West Germanic *singwan, from Proto-Germanic *singwaną (“to sing”), from Proto-Indo-European *sengʷʰ- (“to recite, sing”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian sjunge (“to sing”), West Frisian sjonge (“to sing”), Dutch zingen (“to sing”), German Low German singen (“to sing”), German singen (“to sing”), Danish and Norwegian Bokmål synge (“to sing”), Swedish sjunga (“to sing”), Norwegian Nynorsk, Faroese, and Icelandic syngja (“to sing”), Ancient Greek ὀμφή (omphḗ, “voice, oracle”).

ex.en: She doesn't like to sing a sad song.
ex.ja: 彼女は悲しい歌を歌うのは嫌いだ。

ex.en: Have you ever heard her sing on stage?
ex.ja: ステージ上での彼女の歌を聴いたことがありますか？

ex.en: In the park birds are singing all around.
ex.ja: 公園ではいたるところで小鳥がさえずっている。

note.ja: 古英語 singan から。song は名詞形。

en: Any physical device meant to ease or do a task.
Any piece of equipment used in a profession, such as a craftsman's.
To work on or shape with tools, e.g., hand-tooled leather.
To equip with tools.

tool.ety: From Middle English tool, tol, from Old English tōl (“tool, implement, instrument”, literally “that with which one prepares something”), perhaps borrowed from Old Norse tól, but at any rate ultimately from Proto-Germanic *tōlą (“that which is used in preparation, tool”), from Proto-Indo-European *dewh₂- (“to tie to, secure”), equivalent to taw (“to prepare”) + -le (agent suffix). Cognate with Scots tuil (“tool, implement, instrument, device”), Icelandic tól (“tool”), Faroese tól (“tool, instrument”). Related to Old English tāwian (“to make, prepare, or cultivate”); see taw, and tow ("fibres us

ex.en: These tools are used for building a house.
ex.ja: これらの道具は家を建てるのに使われる。

ex.en: These tools are badly in need of repair.
ex.ja: これらの道具には本当に修理が必要だ。

ex.en: They used tools similar to those used there.
ex.ja: 彼らはそこで使われていた道具に類似した道具を使っていた。

en: Capturing the overall sense of a thing.
Characteristically representing something by form, group, idea or type.
Anything that is typical, normal, or standard.

typical.ety: From Late Latin typicalis, from Latin typicus (“typical”), from Ancient Greek τυπικός (tupikós, “of or pertaining to a type, conformable, typical”), from τύπος (túpos, “mark, impression, type”), equivalent to typic + -al and type + -ical.

ex.en: It was typical of him to arrive late.
ex.ja: 遅れてやってくるのは、いかにも彼のやりそうなことだった。

ex.en: She took a typical example of modern music.
ex.ja: 彼女は近代音楽の典型的な例を挙げた。

ex.en: He seems to be a typical American boy.
ex.ja: 彼は典型的なアメリカの少年のようだ。

note.ja: type（型）+ -ical。ギリシャ語 typos（打ち跡）。「型どおりの」→「典型的な」。

en: The sum of everything that exists in the cosmos.
An entity similar to our universe; one component of a larger entity known as the multiverse.

universe.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *h₁óynos
Proto-Italic *oinos
Old Latin oinos

From Middle English universe, from Old French univers, from Latin universum (“all things, as a whole, the universe”), neuter of universus (“all together, whole, entire, collective, general, literally turned or combined into one”), from uni-, combining form of unus (

ex.en: There are millions of stars in the universe.
ex.ja: 宇宙には何百万もの星がある。

ex.en: I wonder if we're alone in the universe.
ex.ja: 宇宙には僕らしかいないんだろうか？

ex.en: What is the origin of the universe?
ex.ja: 宇宙の始まりは何ですか。

note.ja: ラテン語 universum ＝ unus（ひとつ）+ versus（回された）。「ひとつにまとめられたもの」→「宇宙」。university と同じ。

en: To make (someone) aware of impending danger, evil, etc.
To notify or inform (someone, about something).

warn.ety: From Middle English warnen, warnien (“to warn; admonish”), from Old English warnian (“to take heed; warn”), from Proto-Germanic *warnōną (“to warn; take heed”), from Proto-Indo-European *wer- (“to be aware; give heed”). Cognate with Dutch waarnen (obsolete), German Low German warnen, German warnen, Swedish varna, Icelandic varna.

ex.en: You should have paid attention to her warning.
ex.ja: 彼女の警告にきちんと耳を傾ければよかったのに。

ex.en: The radio gave a warning of bad weather.
ex.ja: ラジオは悪天候になると告げた。

ex.en: The others paid no attention to her warning.
ex.ja: 他の人々は彼女の警告に注意を払わなかった。

note.ja: 古英語 warnian から。ware（用心する）と同系。aware、beware と同じ。

en: The fourth day of the week in many religious traditions, and the third day of the week in systems using the ISO 8601 norm; it follows Tue…
On Wednesday.

Wednesday.ety: From Middle English Wednesday, from unattested Old English *wēdnesdæġ (“Wednesday”), synchronically an i-mutated form of attested wōdnesdæġ (itself from Proto-West Germanic *Wōdanas dag, its reflex Middle English Wodnesdei falling into disuse), from Proto-West Germanic *Wōdinas dag also attested in Old Frisian wednesdei and Middle Dutch wenesdach, equivalent to Woden + -s- + day. In any case, a calque (interpretātiō germānica) of Latin diēs Mercuriī (“day of Mercury”) and Koine Ancient Greek ἡμέρα (hēméra, “day”) Ἑρμοῦ (Hermoû, “of Hermes”), via an association of the god Odin (“Woden”) with Me

ex.en: My brother-in-law passed away last Wednesday.
ex.ja: 先週の水曜日、義理の兄が亡くなりました。

ex.en: We go to the park every Wednesday.
ex.ja: 毎週水曜日は、公園に行きます。

ex.en: She has been sick since last Wednesday.
ex.ja: 彼女は先週の水曜日から病気です。

note.ja: 古英語 Wōdnesdæg（主神オーディンの日）。ラテン語 dies Mercurii（メルクリウスの日）を置き換えた。

en: To allow to enter; to grant entrance (to), whether into a place, into the mind, or into consideration.
To allow (someone) to enter a profession or to enjoy a privilege; to recognize as qualified for a franchise.

admit.ety: From Middle English admitten, amitten, borrowed from Old French admettre, amettre (“to admit”), from Latin admittō (“to allow entrance, inlet”, literally “to send to”), from ad- + mittere (“to send”).

ex.en: The man admitted having broken into the house.
ex.ja: 男はその家に押し入ったことを認めた。

ex.en: He'll never admit to being in the wrong.
ex.ja: 彼は自分が悪いことをしても、決して認めようとしない。

ex.en: There are people who can't admit they're wrong.
ex.ja: 自分の非を認めない人っているよね。

note.ja: ad（〜へ）+ mit（送る）。中へ送り入れる →「入ることを許す・認める」。

en: The position of the body or way of carrying oneself.
A disposition or state of mind.
To assume or to place in a particular position or orientation; to pose.
To express an attitude through one's posture, bearing, tone of voice, etc.

attitude.ety: From French attitude, from Italian attitudine (“attitude, aptness”), from Medieval Latin aptitūdō (“aptitude”) and actitūdō (“acting, posture”), from Latin aptō and actitō. Doublet of aptitude.

ex.en: I think that belief depends on good attitude.
ex.ja: そう思うのは、心の持ちようだと思います。

ex.en: I don't like his attitude. Stop seeing him.
ex.ja: あの男は感じが悪い。彼と付き合うのは止めろ。

ex.en: The attitude holds good in such a situation.
ex.ja: その態度はその状況においては有効だ。

note.ja: イタリア語 attitudine（姿勢）から。ラテン語 aptitudo（適性）。aptitude と同じ語源。「体の構え」→「心の構え」。

en: The woody part of a tree arising from the trunk and usually dividing.
Any of the parts of something that divides like the branch of a tree.
To arise from the trunk or a larger branch of a tree.
To produce branches.

branch.ety:
From Middle English branche, braunche, bronche, from Old French branche, branke, from Late Latin branca (“footprint”, later also “paw, claw”) (whence Middle High German pranke, German Pranke (“paw”)), of unknown origin.
Perhaps of Celtic origin, from a hypothetical Gaulish *vranca, from Proto-Indo-European *wrónk-eh₂. If so, then Indo-European cognates include Old Norse rá, vró (“angle, corner”), and possibly Lithuanian rankà (“hand”), Old Church Slavonic рѫка (rǫka, “hand”), Albanian rangë (“yardwork”).
The verb is from Middle English braunchen, from the noun.

ex.en: The large chain store created a new branch.
ex.ja: その大チェーンストアは新しく支店を作った。

ex.en: Will you take this document to the branch?
ex.ja: この書類を支社に届けてくれませんか。

ex.en: He cut off a branch from the tree.
ex.ja: 彼は木から枝を切り離した。

note.ja: ラテン語 branca（足・爪）から古フランス語を経た語。「枝」→「支店・部門」。

en: The hard, brown wood of a certain species of the tribe Caesalpinieae; originally sappan (Biancaea sappan), of the East Indies, and later …
A Brazil nut.

ex.en: Soccer is the most popular sport in Brazil.
ex.ja: サッカーはブラジルで最も人気のあるスポーツだ。

ex.en: Brazil is the country I was born in.
ex.ja: ブラジルは、私の生まれ故郷です。

ex.en: Football is the most popular sport in Brazil.
ex.ja: サッカーはブラジルで最も人気のあるスポーツだ。

note.ja: ポルトガル語 pau-brasil（赤い染料の木）から。brasa（燃えさし）。その木が多く採れる土地 →「ブラジル」。

en: The act or method of controlling or directing.
Skillful guidance or management.
To lead; to direct; to be in charge of (people or tasks)
To behave.

conduct.ety: From Late Latin conductus (“defense, escort”), from Latin conductus, perfect passive participle of condūcō (“bring together”); see also conduce. Displaced native Old English þēaw. Doublet of conduit.

ex.en: We ask you to account for your conduct.
ex.ja: あなたの行為の責任をもってもらおう。

ex.en: We conducted our investigation with the greatest care.
ex.ja: 私たちはきわめて慎重に調査を行なった。

ex.en: A guide conducted the visitors round the museum.
ex.ja: ガイドは観光客に博物館の案内をした。

note.ja: con（共に）+ duct（導く）。一緒に導く →「行う・指揮する・行い」。

en: A group, set, or series of ten , particularly
A period of ten years , particularly such a period beginning with a year ending in 0 and ending with a year ending in 9.

decade.ety: From Middle English decade, from Old French decade, from Late Latin decādem (“(set of) ten”), from Ancient Greek δεκάς (dekás), from δέκα (déka, “ten”). In reference to a span of ten years, originally a clipping of the phrase decade of years. By surface analysis, dec- + -ade. Doublet of decad and dekad.

ex.en: I lost my son about a decade ago.
ex.ja: 私は息子を約十年前に亡くした。

ex.en: This tree has been standing for five decades.
ex.ja: この木は５０年間ここに立っている。

ex.en: He has had that job for decades.
ex.ja: 彼はあの仕事を何十年もしている。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 dekas（10のまとまり）から。deka（10）。「10年間」。decimal と同系。

en: To set apart for a deity or for religious purposes; consecrate.
To set apart for a special use.
One who dedicates themselves, or who is dedicated, to the service of some leader, religion, etc.

dedicate.ety: From Middle English dedicaten (“to dedicate”), from dedicat(e) (“dedicated”, also used as the past participle of dedicaten) + -en (verb-forming suffix), from Latin dēdicātus, the perfect passive participle of dēdicō (“to dedicate, proclaim”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix).

ex.en: The author dedicated the book to his sister.
ex.ja: 著者はその本を姉にささげた。

ex.en: His brother dedicated his life to the activity.
ex.ja: 彼の兄はその活動に命を捧げた。

ex.en: He dedicated his life to helping the poor.
ex.ja: 彼は生涯を貧しい人々を救う事に捧げた。

note.ja: ラテン語 dedicare ＝ de + dicare（宣言する）。「（神に）ささげると宣言する」→「ささげる」。dictate と同系。

en: A statement of the meaning of a word, word group, sign, or symbol; especially, a dictionary definition.
A clear instance conforming to the dictionary or textbook definition.

definition.ety: From Middle English diffinicioun, from Middle French definition, from Latin dēfīnītiō, from dēfīniō. Equivalent to define + -ition.

ex.en: Look up the definition of 'guy' in your dictionary.
ex.ja: 君の辞書で‘ｇｕｙ’の語義を調べなさい。

ex.en: What is the definition of lifestyle disease?
ex.ja: 生活習慣病の定義は何ですか？

ex.en: Can you give me the definition of a cone?
ex.ja: 円錐形の定義を教えてくれませんか。

note.ja: define（定義する）+ -ition。de + finis（境界）。「境界をはっきりさせること」→「定義・鮮明さ」。

en: A kind or helpful deed; an instance of voluntarily assisting (someone).
Goodwill; benevolent regard.
To look upon fondly; to prefer.
To use more often.

ex.en: Are you in favor of the new law?
ex.ja: あなたはその新しい法律に賛成ですか。

ex.en: All those in favor held up their hands.
ex.ja: 賛成の人は皆手を挙げた。

ex.en: I need to ask you for a favor.
ex.ja: 一つお願いがあります。

en: A piece of cloth, often decorated with an emblem, used as a visual signal or symbol.
The design that could be placed on a flag, typically a rectangular graphic that is used to represent an entity (like a country, organisat…
To furnish or deck out with flags.
To mark with a flag, especially to indicate the importance of something.

flag.ety:
From Middle English flag, flagge (“flag”), further etymology uncertain. Perhaps from or related to early Middle English flage (name for a baby's garment) and Old English flagg, flacg (“cataplasm, poultice, plaster”). Or, perhaps ultimately imitative, or otherwise drawn from Proto-Germanic *flaką (“something flat”), from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat, broad, plain”), referring to the shape.
Germanic cognates include Saterland Frisian Flaage (“flag”), West Frisian flagge (“flag”), Dutch vlag (“flag”), German Flagge (“flag”), Swedish flagga (“flag”), Danish flag (“flag, ship's flag”). Compar

ex.en: The French flag is blue, white and red.
ex.ja: フランスの国旗は青、白、赤です。

ex.en: The ship was flying the American flag.
ex.ja: その船はアメリカ国旗を掲げていた。

ex.en: What do the stars mean on the flag of Brazil?
ex.ja: ブラジル国旗の星にはどういう意味があるんですか？

note.ja: 16世紀からの語。語源ははっきりしない。「旗」→ 目印の「フラグ」。

en: To fit, as for a specific end or purpose; make suitable or comfortable; adapt; adjust.
To construct by fitting together or uniting various parts; fabricate by union of constituent parts.
The structural elements of a building or other constructed object.
Anything composed of parts fitted and united together; a fabric; a structure.

frame.ety:
From Middle English framen, fremen, fremmen (“to construct, build, strengthen, refresh, perform, execute, profit, avail”), from Old English framian, fremian, fremman (“to profit, avail, advance”), from Proto-West Germanic *frammjan, from Proto-Germanic *framjaną (“to further, promote, perform”), from Proto-Indo-European *promo- (“front, forward”).
Cognate with Low German framen (“to commit, effect”), Danish fremme (“to promote, further, perform”), Swedish främja (“to promote, encourage, foster”), Icelandic fremja (“to commit”). More at from.

ex.en: The frame of the building is now complete.
ex.ja: その建物の骨組みは今や完成している。

ex.en: This is a picture frame made of plastic.
ex.ja: これはプラスチック製の額縁です。

ex.en: This frame shows the painting to good advantage.
ex.ja: この額に入れると絵が引き立ちます。

en: A recipient of hospitality, especially someone staying by invitation at the house of another.
A patron or customer in a hotel etc.
To appear as a guest, especially on a broadcast.
As a musician: to play as a guest, providing an instrument that a band/orchestra does not normally have in its line up (for instance, per…

guest.ety:
From Middle English gest, from Old Norse gestr, which replaced or was merged with Old English ġiest, both from Proto-Germanic *gastiz, from Proto-Indo-European *gʰóstis (“stranger, guest, host, someone with whom one has reciprocal duties of hospitality”). Doublet of host, from Latin.

ex.en: Our guests should be here within an hour.
ex.ja: お客様は１時間以内にお越しになるはずです。

ex.en: I'd like you to be my guest tonight.
ex.ja: 今夜は私の家にお泊まりください。

ex.en: The hotel has a lot of foreign guests.
ex.ja: ホテルには外国人が多い。

note.ja: 古北欧語 gestr から。ラテン語 hostis（よそ者・敵）、host と同じ祖先。

en: The abode of God and of the angels and saints in His presence.
The abode of the Abrahamic God; similar abodes of the gods in other religions and traditions, such as Mount Olympus.

heaven.ety:
From a wide variety of Middle English forms including hevene, heven, hevin, and hewin (“heaven, sky”), from Old English heofon, heofone (“heaven, sky”), from Proto-West Germanic *hebn (“heaven, sky”), of uncertain origin.
Cognate with Scots heiven, hewin (“heaven, sky”), Middle Dutch heven (“sky, heaven”), Low German Heven (“heaven, sky”), and possibly the rare Icelandic and Old Norse hifinn (“heaven, sky”), which are all probably dissimilated forms of the Germanic root which appears in Old Norse himinn (“heaven, sky”), Gothic 𐌷𐌹𐌼𐌹𐌽𐍃 (himins, “heaven, sky”), Old Swedish himin, Old Danish himæn

ex.en: Lord Jesus Christ in heaven, please protect me.
ex.ja: 天国にいらつしやる基督様。どうか私を御守り下さいまし。

ex.en: For the love of Heaven, don't get angry.
ex.ja: お願いだから、怒らないでください。

ex.en: Do you want to go to heaven with me?
ex.ja: 一緒に天国へ行きたいか？

note.ja: 古英語 heofon から。「空」→「天国」。

en: The quality or state of being independent; lack of dependence; the state of not being reliant on, or controlled by, others.
The state of having sufficient means for a comfortable livelihood.
